title: Vegetarian Borscht with White Beans and Dill
summary: A hearty meat-free borscht of beetroot and carrot matchsticks, potato, cabbage and white beans in a sweet-sour tomato broth, served with sour cream and dill.
equipment: large heavy pot (about 5 litres) with lid

ingredients.item: raw beetroot (about 3), peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
can cannellini or white beans, drained and rinsed
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soften the base
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 min, then add the carrot and beetroot and stir for 10 min until the beetroot softens and the oil turns deep red.

steps.title: Add the flavourings
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and paprika and cook 2 min. Add 1 tbsp of the vinegar now, which keeps the colour bright.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Pour in the water, add the bay and potatoes and bring to the boil. Cover and simmer 15 min.

steps.title: Add cabbage and beans
steps.text: Add the cabbage, beans and salt and simmer, uncovered, for 10 min more, until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.

steps.title: Balance
steps.text: Stir in the remaining vinegar and the sugar. Taste: it should be gently sweet-sour. Rest the soup, covered and off the heat, for 10 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle into bowls, add a spoon of sour cream and scatter with dill and pepper.

tips: A splash of vinegar early on keeps the beetroot a vivid red.
Like most borscht, it tastes even better the next day.
Wear gloves when cutting beetroot to avoid stained hands.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze (without the sour cream) for up to 3 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
